## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The new `--exclude` flag needs an `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` environment-variable default, because the project's CLI flag policy requires one for every new flag under `cli/`. That is the only open finding, and it is Important.

## Changes
This pull request adds a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` flag. `collect()` uses `fnmatch` to skip files whose basename matches a pattern. The change also documents the flag in `docs/flags.md`, adds parser, collection and end-to-end archive tests, and adds a one-line text fixture under `tests/fixtures/`.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- cli/main.py:17 — correctness — Read the --exclude default from ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE — With `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE='*.log'` set and no `--exclude` argument, `.log` files are still archived because the default is hard-coded to `[]`. This breaks `.claude/skills/cli-flags/SKILL.md:11`: "Every command-line flag added under `cli/` from now on must also take its default from an `ARCHIVE_<NAME>` environment variable". — CI jobs that set options through the environment cannot exclude files and will silently archive everything. — Fix: Derive the default from `os.environ.get("ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE")`, choose and document a separator for multiple globs, update the default column in `docs/flags.md:7`, and extend `test_exclude_defaults_to_nothing` to cover the variable.
